CASE STUDY

I ran an AI agent on 100 apps. Here is how well it did.

The agent reads each app's website and docs and answers 6 questions about whether Composio can build a connector for it. About half of its answers were right.

95/100
apps researched. 5 failed because of AI service errors.
49.5%
answers correct (53 of 107) against the answer key. Same in both runs.
29/50
apps in run 2 have at least one answer the agent marked "not sure".

8 answers got worse in run 2

  • 5 answers — the agent added an extra item to a list (e.g. "REST, GraphQL" instead of "REST"). Strict scoring marks the whole answer wrong. The extra items were not checked one by one. (DealCloud, Zendesk, Sherlock, WhatsApp Business, PitchBook)
  • 2 answers — fanbasis went from right to "unknown". Its docs are on a different website (commasdocs.com) and the agent never found them.
  • 1 answer — Waterfall.io went from "unknown" to a wrong guess.

Hand check

I checked 8 apps by hand

13 answers on HubSpot, Close, Copper, GitHub, Notion, Jira, Linear and Clay. The agent had marked 7 of the 8 as "not sure". Copper was not marked.

6 wrong
3 weak
4 correct
Wrong or missedProof is weakHeld up

Wrong or missed (6)

  • GitHub, Notion, Jira, Linear, Clay: agent said "unknown" AI connector. All 5 have an official one.
  • Copper: agent said "none". An official one is announced (not public yet), and community-made ones exist.

Proof is weak (3)

  • Close "paid plan needed": pricing page shows a free trial that seems to include API access.
  • Close "bearer token" login: API key page says username/password style.
  • HubSpot: one old quote used for 3 answers.

Held up (4)

  • HubSpot official AI connector
  • Close official AI connector
  • Copper login methods
  • HubSpot bearer token
  • Key lesson: "not marked" does not mean correct. Copper was wrong with no warning.
  • These 8 were picked because they looked doubtful, so this is not an error rate for all 50 apps.
  • The other 21 marked apps are not checked yet. Notes: data/human_review_notes.md.

Limits

What to keep in mind

  • About half the answers are right. Not ready for real use without a person checking.
  • The answer key is small: 20 apps, and only 7 for the AI-connector question.
  • The proof check only sees if a quote exists on the page, not if it supports the answer.
  • Some "unknown" answers can never trigger a retry. 31 were never retried for this reason.
  • "Not marked as unsure" does not mean correct (Copper).
  • The Composio check is by name only. It shows a toolkit exists, not how complete it is.

Next steps (planned, not done yet)

  • Let "unknown" API-size and AI-connector answers trigger a retry.
  • Check each item in a list answer has its own proof.
  • Search for docs on other websites, not just the product site (the fanbasis case).
  • Hand check the other 21 marked apps and the low-confidence answers, then re-score.
  • Run run 2 on the other 50 apps when free limits allow.
Technical details
  • Answer key: drafted from official docs; I verified 15 of the 20 apps myself.
  • Checks D1–D4: D1 quote is on the page, D2 trusted source, D3 page loaded, D4 fields agree. Run 1 numbers cover 45 apps, because the other 5 of the 50 failed in run 1.
  • Why D4 got worse: D4 checks 3 rules: access vs buildability, api_type vs main_blocker, and existing_mcp_status vs existing_mcp_url. On the 45 apps in both runs, run 1 had 21 apps with MCP status official/community (7 missing a URL), and run 2 had 20 (11 missing a URL). That explains the rise from 8 to 11 within those 45. The rest of the jump to 14 comes from Xero, Fathom and Reducto (not researched in run 1), which run 2 also marked official/community with no URL. Run 2 does not claim an MCP server more often. It just leaves out the URL more often. The cause was not measured.
  • Gemini-only subset: the 9 answer-key apps whose run 1 record also came from Gemini went from 29/49 to 31/49. That's too few to call an improvement.
  • Confidence in run 1: no "high" level; medium 52/88 (59.1%), low 1/19 (5.3%).
  • Rate limits: 12 Gemini "too many requests" (429) errors in run 2. All were retried by Google's own client library, so this project's own wait-60s-and-stop logic was not exercised.
  • Unsure fields in run 1: 49 of 95 apps have at least one unknown or low-confidence field (147 fields in total). These are gaps the agent admitted, not silent guesses.
  • Failed apps: 5 apps have no record (QuickBooks, Xero, Otter AI, Fathom, Reducto). All failed because of AI provider errors during extraction, not missing data on the web.
  • Models in run 1: gemini-3.5-flash-lite (48 apps), openai/gpt-oss-120b, qwen/qwen3.8-27b. Qwen's records are clearly less reliable, a result of switching providers under free-limit pressure.
  • API calls: Groq 126 (exact). Gemini in run 1 was not counted exactly: at least 2 per completed app (~96), excluding retries. Run 2: about 310 Gemini requests (counted by the pipeline), including retries.
  • Composio check: done by hand with Claude in Chrome after run 1, against 1,841 toolkits. Short names that could be another product (Close, Front, Plain, Copper, Clay, Grain, Consensus, Ramp) were checked by reading the toolkit description. The agent's own catalog check never ran.
  • Hand check notes: for the 5 "unknown" apps I looked at Google results, not the vendors' own pages, so server URLs are not confirmed. URLs for HubSpot and Close were not found on the pages I opened. The data files were not changed.
Words used on this page
API — a way for software to talk to an app
MCP server / AI connector — a ready-made plug that lets AI agents use an app
OAuth — "Log in with…" style permission
API key / bearer token — a secret code sent with each request
REST / GraphQL — two common styles of API
Toolkit — Composio's connector for an app
Answer key — correct answers for 20 apps, from official docs
Run 1 / Run 2 — pass 1 and pass 2 in the repo
